explanations: In BoxlyAdapter.toEntry, `modifiedAt: new Date(c.modified_unix)` passes a Unix timestamp in seconds to the Date constructor, which expects milliseconds. Every remote entry gets a modifiedAt in January 1970, so in planSync the check `entry.modifiedAt > local.modifiedAt` is false for any file that already exists locally: changed remote files whose local copy has no edits are silently never downloaded. The fix is `new Date(c.modified_unix * 1000)`. The adapter boundary is exactly where provider units must be converted to domain units.

request() returns only when res.ok; otherwise it reads the body text and throws ProviderError with res.status. retryable is true only for 429 or >= 500, so 409 is non-retryable. No empty page is returned, and res.json() is never reached because request() throws first.

All requests go through request(), which passes AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs). The abort rejects fetch, and the catch block wraps it as ProviderError with status 0 and retryable true. There is no synthetic 504 and the adapter itself does no retries.

After each page, planSync saves page.nextCursor before fetching the next page. After page two finishes, the saved cursor points at page three, so a restart re-lists page three. Cursors are saved incrementally, not at the end, and the third page's own nextCursor is never saved because the crash happens before that line.
